speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: The SDA provides powers to regulate the construction, maintenance, improvement, operation and use of sewerage and drainage systems and the discharge of sewage and trade effluent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Over the past decades, the SDA has allowed the Public Utilities Board (PUB) to regulate discharges into our sewerage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This ensures that the used water received at our Water Reclamation Plants or WRPs, can be effectively and efficiently treated and sent to the NEWater Factories for further treatment to produce NEWater.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: NEWater, an ultra-clean, high-grade reclaimed water, plays a critical role in Singapore's water supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: It is delivered to key customers like wafer fabrication plants and is also used to top up our reservoirs during dry spells.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We have also taken steps to improve our stormwater drainage system over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: In 2008, we completed the Marina Reservoir by damming up the Singapore River.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This alleviated flooding in the low-lying areas in the city centre and provided us with a new source of catchment water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Over the years, we have continued to develop innovative drainage solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Just this September, we marked the opening of Alkaff Lake at Bidadari Park, which not only functions as a stormwater retention pond to prevent floods in the Bidadari Estate during heavy rain, but also serves as a recreational space to bring people closer to water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: As a weather-resilient National Tap less affected by dry spells, NEWater's importance will thus grow and we must take further steps to protect the quality of our used water which affects how we are able to treat it into NEWater.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We will also need to ensure that our stormwater drainage system continues to be protected and kept in good working order, so that it can withstand more frequent extreme weather events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Our proposed amendments to the SDA seek to achieve these two objectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Better secure our used water system and in turn safeguard the production of NEWater; and also enhance our flood resilience by better protecting the stormwater drainage system and keeping it in proper working order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We will also introduce amendments related to PUB's operations, to better support their operational needs as Singapore's national water agency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: As Singapore develops further, our sewerage system will also expand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Last year, PUB completed tunnelling works for Phase 2 of the DTSS, comprising 98 km of deep tunnels and link sewers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Our sewerage system channels used water from industries and households to our water reclamation plants which provide the treated used water as feedstock to our NEWater factories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: To better secure our NEWater supply, we must leverage technology to better protect the sewerage system and take stronger actions against illegal discharges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: A key feature of the Bill is to support the use of technology to better protect our sewerage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: General Waste Collectors (GWCs) collect sewage, greasy waste and organic sludge for disposal at WRPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Their tankers need to be registered with PUB annually and they are only allowed to collect authorised waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: However, some GWCs may illegally collect unauthorised waste or dispose any collected waste directly into sewers instead of our WRPs to avoid paying for the costs of treatment or disposal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: In 2021, PUB investigated two such cases, but the cases could not be established as PUB was unable to verify their collection routes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: These devices provide GPS tracking and geo-fenced smart-locking capabilities to allow the discharge valves of GWC tankers to only open at designated points in our water reclamation plants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Aside from illegal discharges, our sewerage system is also impacted when contractors physically damage our sewerage system such as when a piling rig punctures a sewer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 42 will also enable regulations to require the installation of tracking devices on piling and soil investigation rigs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This will provide real-time alerts to PUB and contractors if their rigs are near our sewerage system, so that preventive actions can be taken where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 43 enacts a related amendment to the Public Utilities Act 2001 for large water supply pipelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Prior to introducing these measures, PUB engaged the industry to seek their feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: GWCs welcomed the change as they could at the same time use the GPS devices for fleet management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Contractors were also supportive as the GPS devices would help them avoid damaging the sewers during works, which could result in much higher costs and delays.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Since April 2023, the industry has already implemented these requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: All GWC tankers registered with PUB have installed GPS devices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Tracking devices have also been installed on piling and soil investigation rigs deployed to projects in the DTSS or trunk sewer protection corridor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Hence, the amendments seek to regularise these requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: With recent improvements in technology, contractors now have more advanced methods such as probing with plastic drill bits and sonar detection to identify buried services including sewers before carrying out activities like excavation or drilling works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: The industry often prefers these advanced methods as they are less intrusive and more efficient than physically digging a trial trench.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 9 thus provides for PUB's acceptance of such alternative methods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Today, we have a suite of end-to-end measures to deter illegal discharges into the sewerage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Upstream, we have a thorough vetting process before granting approvals for discharge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Our officers conduct regular inspections and monitoring throughout the network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: When illegal discharges are detected, we may issue stop work orders, revoke approvals for trade effluent discharge and impose penalties on offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We also communicate regularly with companies that discharge trade effluent to remind them of the important role that they play in protecting our sewers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: But there are some irresponsible offenders, including some recalcitrant ones, whose actions have threatened our used water system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Toxic and harmful discharge can kill the microorganisms used to treat used water at the WRPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This results in the water being unfit for further treatment at our NEWater factories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: To rectify the impact, PUB would have to temporarily halt the NEWater production process and ramp up other National Taps to make up for these disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Illegal discharges also jeopardise the safety of the people who work hard to maintain our used water system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: When companies illegally discharge high concentrations of volatile organic compounds such as benzene and toluene, workers that maintain our sewers and operate our water reclamation plants may breathe in the toxic fumes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: These highly flammable compounds also create fire and explosion risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Even as PUB takes all necessary measures to ensure the safety of its workers, we should seek to eliminate such hazards in the first place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: PUB also has to expend resources to investigate and carry out extensive sampling to identify the source of the illegal discharge and take remedial actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: To enhance deterrence, we have reviewed the penalties under the SDA and propose to enhance these to ensure the penalty regime remains effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We will implement changes in two areas: raise maximum penalties and introduce mandatory minimum penalties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: First, penalties should better reflect the severe impact to our water supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Irresponsible actions can cause disruptions to the NEWater production process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: They can also endanger workers operating and maintaining our used water sewerage system and working at our WRPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Therefore, the penalties should better reflect the gravity of such irresponsible actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This is done both by raising the maximum penalty and introducing minimum penalties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Second, the penalty quanta should be substantial enough so that companies are not incentivised to flout the law instead of taking the necessary measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Third, the penalty quanta should be generally aligned with those of similar offences in other Acts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: For example, we aligned the maximum penalties in the SDA with that of similar offences in the Environmental Protection and Management Act 1999.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: In setting the minimum penalty quanta, we also considered that several Acts had mandatory minimum penalties of about 20% of the maximum penalty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: The first enhancement is to raise maximum penalties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 42 will amend section 74(2) to double the maximum penalty from $15,000 to $30,000 for repeat offences under regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Penalties for sewerage offences, such as carrying out unauthorised sewerage works, will also be raised to match corresponding increases in penalties for drainage offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: These actions impact the conveyance capacity of our sewers and may result in leaks or even sewer overflows, which pose public health and environmental pollution risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 7 will amend section 11(4) to increase the maximum first-offence penalties for the alteration of sewerage system without approval, from $20,000 to $50,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Maximum penalties for repeat offenders will be increased from $20,000 to $100,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 10 will amend section 14(4) to increase maximum first-offence penalties for carrying out works affecting or likely to affect the sewer or sewerage system without approval, from $20,000 to $50,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Maximum penalties for repeat offenders will be increased from $20,000 to $100,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 17 will amend section 20(1) to increase the maximum first offence penalties for the damage caused to a public sewerage system, from $40,000 to $50,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Maximum penalties for repeat offenders will be increased from $40,000 to $100,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 13 will amend section 16A(5) to insert a mandatory minimum penalty for discharging dangerous or hazardous substances into any public sewerage system without PUB's approval or not in accordance with the conditions of that approval or regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Mandatory minimum penalties will be set at $10,000 for the first offence, and $20,000 for the second offence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 13 will amend section 16A(6) to insert a minimum penalty for discharging dangerous or hazardous substances without approval or not in accordance with the conditions of that approval or regulations, which causes injury, death, damage to sewers or disruption to treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This will be set at $40,000 for the first offence, and $80,000 for repeat offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 14 will amend section 17(4) to insert a minimum penalty for failing to comply with an order to stop and treat discharge of hazardous substances into the public sewerage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: There are other offences in legislation with minimum penalties, such as the Prevention of Pollution of the Sea Act 1990, which has a minimum penalty for the discharge of oil or oily mixture from ships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: While the intent of the amendments to the penalty regime is to increase deterrence, we recognise that this measure cannot work in isolation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: PUB will continue to work closely with companies, including through engagement sessions to share best practices, to ensure that their trade effluent is managed and discharged responsibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Next, let me move on to the amendments intended to enhance flood resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: In Singapore, we adopt a holistic "Source-Pathway-Receptor" approach to manage stormwater.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: At source, we try to slow down surface runoff at developments to reduce peak flow into public drains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: At locations where stormwater runoff is generated, we require new developments of more than 0.2 hectares to implement solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Solutions could include detention tanks or nature-based solutions to slow down stormwater run-off entering the public drainage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Along the pathways or the routes through which stormwater is conveyed, PUB designs drains and canals to convey stormwater efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: To enhance our pathways, we raised design standards for drains in 2011 to cater for more intense rainfall events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We also implemented important drainage improvement projects like the Stamford Diversion Canal for this purpose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: For example, Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station entrances are required to be elevated above ground level with a minimum crest level to prevent stormwater from entering the MRT stations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: The stormwater drainage is one continuous system – actions affecting one part of the system can have severe impact elsewhere in the system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: To provide an example, in 2021, there was a construction firm that was doing road-widening works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: In the process, they blocked off a roadside drain and diverted the flow to a new drain section that was still under construction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: They did so without PUB's approval and this irresponsible action eventually led to a flood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Traffic came to a standstill for about two hours, 13 vehicles were partially submerged and one person was taken to hospital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: The proposed amendments will introduce measures across the system to improve stormwater management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: The capacity and function of drains and reservoirs can be compromised due to unauthorised modifications or obstructions caused by debris and silt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This can cause stormwater to back up and flood surrounding developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We will raise penalties to deter damage or unauthorised modifications to the stormwater drainage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clauses 21 and 22 amend sections 23(4) and 24(4) respectively to increase the maximum first-offence penalties for the alteration of stormwater drainage system without approval and interfering with drains that cause flow obstructions respectively, from $20,000 to $50,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Maximum penalties for repeat offenders will be increased from $20,000 to $100,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We aligned the penalty quantum to that of section 26 which relates to works affecting the stormwater drainage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 23 amends section 26(5) to double the maximum penalty for repeat offenders who carry out works or activities which could affect any stormwater drainage system or lead to the discharge of silt directly or indirectly into any stormwater drainage system from $50,000 to $100,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 24 amends section 30(2) to increase the maximum penalty for first offences for causing damage to the stormwater drainage system from $40,000 to $50,000 and raises the maximum penalty for repeat offenders from $40,000 to $100,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We want to be comprehensive and consistent in our coverage of activities that may affect the stormwater drainage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Currently, the SDA only regulates construction activities that affect the stormwater drainage system and non-construction activities in State Land drainage reserves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 22 expands the SDA to also prohibit non-construction activities that cause obstruction to all drains, including those outside of state land drainage reserves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: PUB has silt control powers for the discharge of surface water containing silt from construction activities into the stormwater drainage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: However, non-construction activities, such as sand stockpiles for landscaping works, also have the potential to cause silty discharge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: For example, we have seen a case of a contractor improperly storing material like soil and sand near Punggol Reservoir, resulting in silt being washed into the reservoir during rain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: With more intense weather events, it is not feasible to expand our drains to cater for every extreme rainfall event.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Premises owners and occupiers have a part to play in ensuring the flood resilience of their own premises, which also affects the surrounding developments and connected drainage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 42 amends section 74 to enable regulations to be prescribed towards these requirements in relation to flood protection measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: For example, requiring minimum platform levels at new developments and redevelopments, and requiring crest levels for all entrances, exits or openings to basements or underground structures like tunnels and underground MRT stations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: It has been 12 years since the last Sewerage and Drainage (Amendment) Bill was passed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: These amendments update the SDA provisions so that they stay relevant and effective in supporting PUB's operations in today's context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Currently, PUB is unable to recover the costs if it steps in to carry out rectification works, even when it is clear that the damage was caused by the irresponsible party.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: PUB can only recover costs if the party responsible for the damage had first defaulted on PUB's written notice to perform rectification works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 33 amends section 43 to ensure that PUB officers have powers of entry to deal with emergency situations involving public sewerage systems and stormwater drainage systems, such as chokes or pipes that had developed structural defects over time, so that PUB can undertake urgent rectification work necessary for the service or safety of the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This amendment mirrors existing powers of entry in emergency situations in the Public Utilities Act 2001.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Emergency situations are those that involve damage or obstruction to a public sewerage system or stormwater drainage system where PUB assesses that rectification work is necessary for the service or safety of the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 34 amends section 44A to allow officers to take videos in addition to photographs and require the production of video surveillance footage, during investigations to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Works to sewerage and drainage systems must be completed in accordance with plans approved by PUB, to protect public safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 29 will amend section 36 to clarify who are the owners or occupiers of premises who may be directed to carry out rectification works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This is aligned with the existing provisions for sewerage matters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: I spoke earlier about protecting our sewerage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clauses 9 and 10 will amend sections 13A and 14 respectively to regularise our existing practice of protecting sewers under construction and constructed sewers that have not yet been commissioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: The clauses will require companies to ascertain locations of such sewers to prevent damage to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 42 amends section 74 to empower regulations to be made for the issue of stop work orders so as to stop the discharge of trade effluent, when needed to protect the public sewerage system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: When taking over public drains or sewers constructed by other agencies and developers, PUB needs to impose a Defects Liability Period (DLP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 27 amends section 33 to formally allow PUB to impose the DLP and to provide PUB with recourse should defects arise during the DLP or any warranty against defects is not assigned to PUB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 41 inserts a new section 73A which allows PUB to issue administrative exemptions from legislated requirements on a case-by-case basis, in instances where stakeholders face specific compliance constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: For example, new developments with a small footprint might not be able to meet PUB's Minimum Platform Level requirement as this could lead to additional measures, such as ramps required for barrier-free access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: In such cases, PUB may allow the installation of flood protection systems, like flood barriers, to give the same level of flood protection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: Clause 40 amends section 70 to provide for composition sums collected by PUB under the SDA to be paid into the Consolidated Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: We must also protect our stormwater system to enhance flood resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
text: This will prepare us to adapt to extreme weather patterns that will come with climate change.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This includes those from Lentor Estate and Yio Chu Kang Gardens.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some are worried about the implications of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I acknowledge the Bill's aim to clarify and strengthen our sewage and drainage systems, I seek clarification on several aspects.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These aspects could impact my constituents and the broader community.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, the requirement for homeowners to maintain their sewerage and drainage systems may pose a considerable financial burden.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For many middle-income residents and seniors with no fixed incomes, these costs can represent a significant strain.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Faced with increasing cost of living challenges, some residents may feel compelled to defer or neglect essential maintenance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They may opt for the cheapest quick fix rather than a sustainable long-term solution.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This approach not only jeopardises their properties, but also risks creating problems for their neighbours and the wider community.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, it may lead to disputes with neighbouring property owners who may find themselves compelled to cover the costs or, worse, take legal action to enforce compliance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Such a mechanism would acknowledge the shared responsibility for these critical infrastructure components.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Financial assistance or subsidies should be considered to mitigate potential hardship.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To allow residents ample time to adjust to these new financial responsibilities, could the Government consider a phased implementation of these requirements?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This would provide residents with the opportunity to budget and plan accordingly.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, expanding PUB's authority to access premises without prior notice in emergencies brings up valid concerns regarding the privacy of residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I recognise the importance of swift action in emergencies, we must find a balance between public safety and individual rights.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister elaborate on the specific measures that will be put in place to guarantee transparency and accountability in the exercise of these emergency powers?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clear protocols and oversight mechanisms are essential to prevent potential abuses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To avoid ambiguity and ensure consistent application, could the Government provide more precise guidelines defining what constitutes an "emergency" under the Bill?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In addition, how will residents be informed about such emergency entries?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be a clear process for residents to challenge the necessity of the entry and seek redress if they believe their rights were violated?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Government explore alternative mechanisms, such as requiring warrants in non-life-threatening situations, to balance the need for a rapid response with residents' fundamental right to privacy?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If a resident is not at home during an emergency entry, will there be forced entry?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be any compensation for such an occurrence?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Thirdly, Mr Speaker, permitting PUB to charge fees for assuming the maintenance of specific drainage systems brings up concerns about possible cost hikes for community amenities and facilities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What safeguards will be implemented to prevent excessive fee hikes that could unduly burden residents and community organisations?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To ensure accountability, could we implement transparency requirements mandating PUB to publicly disclose how collected fees are utilised for maintenance and improvements?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, has the Government considered the potential cumulative impact of these fees on Town Councils and the subsequent effect on residents' maintenance fees?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Town Councils manage many shared drainage systems and passing these costs onto residents could create additional financial strain.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Government consider waiving or reducing fees for community-led maintenance initiatives or public amenities that serve the broader community?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This would encourage community involvement and avoid penalising public spaces and activities that are beneficial for everyone.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Since sewage management is a public good, should it not be funded by the Government rather than placing additional costs on residents?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Fourth, Mr Speaker, Sir, empowering PUB to adopt external standards without parliamentary scrutiny may cause some concerns about consistent regulatory compliance for residents and businesses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will PUB ensure that the adopted standards are appropriate for local communities, especially older estates with unique infrastructural challenges?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A one-size-fits-all approach may not be suitable for all areas.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Before adopting external standards, should there be a mechanism for public consultation and feedback to ensure that these standards align with the needs and capacities of local communities and businesses?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What measures will be taken to prevent changes in standards from disproportionately affecting small businesses and homeowners who may have limited resources to adapt to new requirements?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need to work together to create a system that serves the best interests of all residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is not just about policy, it is about people.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I urge the Ministry to carefully consider these clarifications.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Together, we can forge a path forward that is equitable, effective and truly reflective of our commitment to the residents we serve.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The amendments proposed herein are timely, especially since the last Sewerage and Drainage (Amendment) Bill, or in short, SDA, was in 2012.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The first clarification I seek is for the latest statistics.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This will form the backdrop for the enhancement of the penalties sought to be implemented by this Bill.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It will perhaps also elucidate the impetus and necessity for these enhanced penalties.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The enhanced penalties proposed by this Bill, if passed, will strengthen the punitive levers to deter illegal discharge and impose harsher punishments.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The maximum fine of $200,000 will not be changed.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: On the other hand, the maximum fine will be doubled to $400,000.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To this end, while I understand from Senior Minister of State Amy Khor's speech earlier on, on how these fine amounts were derived, such as taking reference from other enforcement statutes, such as the Prevention of Pollution of the Sea Act.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But the more important issue would be that, would this be sufficient to deter the targeted illegality?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While we take care to not exact a punishment that would exceed the crime, this must be balanced against the risk that offenders may simply view any fine as an acceptable business cost.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This will undermine legislative intent as well as public safety.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Just recently, news reports carrying pictures of a river of red flowing through a canal close to Kembangan MRT station.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The sight, by itself, was concerning enough such that members of the public reported it to NEA.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In a 2019 Straits Times news article, PUB had reportedly prosecuted 38 companies in that past year for illegally dumping waste water containing chemicals or other materials into the public sewers. 18 out of those 38 companies, almost half, were repeat offenders.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: According to PUB, trade effluent illegally discharged into public sewers pose significant risks to public health and the environment.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The onus is on the Members of this House to ensure that they, too, get to work under safe and fair conditions.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Thus, I ask the Ministry if we should also consider mandating business owners to take up public liability insurance?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Notwithstanding my clarifications, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have to apologise to you as well, I guess, for whatever I have done.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarification to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the introduction of minimum fines.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mandatory minimum sentences restrict a judge's ability to exercise discretion in determining an appropriate sentence based on the facts before the court.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate that mandatory minimum sentences can send a public signal on the severity of an offence and serve a deterrent effect.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mandatory minimum sentences may also signal the Government's view that the sentences imposed by the courts, thus far, have not been sufficiently high.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, there are less restrictive measures for achieving deterrence and signalling to the court that heavier sentences should be imposed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may include sentencing guidelines by the Sentencing Advisory Panel or even statements from the Minister in Parliament on the severity that certain offences should carry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State elaborate on why it is necessary for these offences to resort to mandatory minimum sentences?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on the recovery of expenses incurred by PUB.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the current Sewerage and Drainage Act, there are provisions for PUB to recover expenses reasonably incurred by PUB, including from persons who fail to comply with PUB's notices and orders or in cases of emergencies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I support such recovery mechanisms based on the polluter pays principle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These provisions ensure that the cost of undoing any damage done is not externalised to taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify what is the intended effect of introducing wording that PUB may recover costs it thinks "just"?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What criteria will PUB apply in determining when it will or will not recover costs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share how actively the existing cost recovery provisions have been utilised?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also share whether PUB's intention is to rely on the cost recovery mechanisms more often in the future?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third and final point is on PUB's powers to enter any premises without notice in cases of emergencies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the current Act, powers to enter without notice may only be exercised for classes of premises declared by the Minister to be liable to inspection without notice or where an authorised officer suspects that an offence was committed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a significant expansion of PUB's powers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State provide more guidance on what situations constitute cases of emergency?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also share which individuals will determine whether there is a case of emergency requiring entry without notice?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Upon entry without notice, is there a time limit within which PUB is required to notify the owners of the entry?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding my clarifications, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any clarifications for Senior Minister of State Khor?
